stories.title: Northmarq Arranges $67M Sale of Two Chicago-Area Apartment Properties
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Midwest Investment Sales team of Parker Stewart, Dominic Martinez, Alex Malzone, and Jake Lamb successfully led the sale of two Chicagoland multifamily apartment communities for a total of $67.25 million. The properties include Westmore Apartments, a 230-unit garden apartment located at 1049 S. Westmore-Meyers Rd. in Lombard, Illinois and Whispering Trails, a 120-unit garden apartment located at 103 S. Testa Dr. in Naperville, Illinois. Northmarq represented the seller, Axiom Properties Inc., for both properties. B & A Property Group, LLC, bought Westmore Apartments for $46 million. FPA Multifamily purchased Whispering Trails for $21.25 million. “The strong interest we saw across both properties reflects the long-term upside of these assets and the quality of their locations within DuPage County,” said Stewart. Built in 1968, Westmore Apartments is a 230-unit garden-style community situated on approximately 11.5 acres in Lombard. The property is currently 98% occupied and offers a mix of one-, two- and three-bedroom floorplans. Whispering Trails, built in 1985, is a 120-unit garden-style community located in the heart of Naperville. The all-two-bedroom community was built in 1985. The post Northmarq Arranges $67M Sale of Two Chicago-Area Apartment Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq sold 350 units across Lombard & Naperville for $67.25M total
Westmore (230 units, 1968) sold for $46M at 98% occupancy in DuPage County
Whispering Trails (120 units, 1985) sold for $21.25M; strong buyer demand signals
stories.summary: Two suburban Chicago multifamily assets—Westmore Apartments (230 units, Lombard) and Whispering Trails (120 units, Naperville)—sold for $67.25M combined, with B&A Property Group and FPA Multifamily as buyers. Westmore achieved 98% occupancy and traded for $46M; Whispering Trails for $21.25M. Strong interest from multiple bidders underscores DuPage County submarket resilience despite asset age (built 1968 and 1985).
stories.impact: Strong sale velocity and pricing in suburban DuPage County (Lombard, Naperville) suggest sustained rental demand and investor confidence in secondary-ring multifamily despite aging stock. This signals a window for value-add or repositioning plays in this submarket before cap rates compress further on quality renovations.

stories.title: Walmart Supercenter to Join Costco, Target in Liberty Hill
stories.excerpt: The town of Liberty Hill only has 13,000 people, but is drawing the attention of some of the nation’s largest retailers. Liberty Hill will soon be home to a Walmart Supercenter. It will have a footprint of 176,246 square feet. The development is expected to cost $12.2 million to build. Construction is expected to begin in late October 2026 and to open its doors in mid-November 2027. Walmart will be part of Santa Rita Ranch Center, a 400,000-square-foot retail project being developed in Santa Rita Ranch. Costco Wholesale opened in Liberty Hill in March 2026, and Target is slated to open on October 11. Other projects earmarked for Liberty Hill include a future Casey’s General Store, a La Tequila Jalisco Mexican restaurant as well as a T.J. Maxx department store. The post Walmart Supercenter to Join Costco, Target in Liberty Hill appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walmart Supercenter 176K SF joining Costco, Target in Liberty Hill, Texas (13K population)
Construction starts late 2026, opens Nov 2027; $12.2M build cost; part of 400K SF retail center
Santa Rita Ranch retail project signals rapid population/retail-anchored growth in small Texas market
stories.summary: Liberty Hill, Texas (population 13,000) is attracting major retail anchors: Costco opened March 2026, Target opens October 2026, and Walmart Supercenter (176K SF) breaks ground late 2026 to open November 2027 as part of the 400K SF Santa Rita Ranch retail center. Additional tenants include Casey's, La Tequila Jalisco, and T.J. Maxx.
stories.impact: Rapid retail concentration in a small exurban Texas market signals underlying population growth and household formation outpacing available retail; multifamily demand likely trails retail by 18–24 months. Developers should scout Liberty Hill and adjacent Austin exurban submarkets for residential sites ahead of retail absorption and the job-center pull it creates.

stories.title: Jewelry Brand Julie Vos Signs 14K-SF Office Lease at 218-232 West 40th Street
stories.excerpt: We gather stones … some to make a diamond ring. Luxury jewelry brand Julie Vos has signed a 14,000-square-foot office lease at Savitt Partners’ 218-232 West 40th Street in Midtown Manhattan, tenant broker Lee & Associates NYC announced Thursday. Julie Vos will occupy the entire fourth floor of the 12-story office building. The length of the lease was not disclosed, but the asking rent was $46 per square foot, according to Lee & Associates. Julie Vos will move employees this month from its current spot at 10 East 38th Street to its new West 40th Street spot, located midblock between Seventh and Eighth avenues. Woody King from Lee represented the tenant, a maker of high-end fashion jewelry, on this deal. “The combination of a private full-floor presence, quality buildout and highly accessible location made this an excellent fit for Julie Vos,” King said in a statement. “The new office gives the company an elevated headquarters that reflects its brand and supports its continued growth.” Brian Neugeboren, Nicole Goetz and Matthew Savitt from Savitt Partners represented the landlord in-house in the deal, using the LLC 218 West 40th Associates. “Today’s office tenants are increasingly focused on finding spaces that can serve multiple functions while reflecting their brand identity,” Savitt said in a statement. “Julie Vos found that opportunity at 218 West 40th Street, and we are pleased to welcome them to the building.” Other tenants at 218 West 40th Street include bra maker Ariela & Associates International and manufacturing company Avery Dennison. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Julie Vos luxury jewelry brand leased 14K SF office at Manhattan's 218-232 West 40th, Midtown
Full fourth-floor lease at $46/SF; relocating from East 38th Street; reflects brand growth
Asks rent $46/SF signals Midtown West strength despite broader Manhattan office headwinds
stories.summary: Julie Vos, a high-end jewelry brand, signed a 14,000-square-foot office lease on the entire fourth floor of Savitt Partners' building at 218-232 West 40th Street (Midtown, between Seventh and Eighth avenues) at an asking rent of $46 per square foot. The company is relocating from its current space at 10 East 38th Street and will move this month.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing dynamics in Manhattan do not directly signal residential demand or supply shifts, and a single luxury-brand relocation is immaterial to market-level apartment underwriting.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Provides $130M Construction Loan for Chicago Multifamily Tower
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Mavrek Development and Fengate Asset Management has secured $130.4 million in construction financing to build a 25-story, 380-unit multifamily tower in Downtown Chicago, Commercial Observer can first report. Affinius Capital provided the debt, while CBRE’s John Parrett arranged the transaction. David Greenburg, managing director and co-head of debt origination at Affinius Capital, described the new project at 1000 West Jackson Street as an “institutional-quality multifamily development,” and noted Chicago’s West Loop has been constrained by low multifamily supply but high population growth due to the renaissance of the Fulton Market neighborhood. “1000 West Jackson pairs proven sponsorship with strong fundamentals, and we look forward to working with Mavrek and Fengate,” he added. Located in Chicago’s West Loop — a live-work-play neighborhood that has seen billions of dollars of new development invested into its real estate in the last decade — the new asset will feature more than 21,500 square feet of ground-floor retail space and divide its residential units between 304 market-rate units and 76 affordable units. The asset will feature approximately 31,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor amenities, including a pool, a fitness center with a basketball court, a resident lounge, coworking spaces, and on-site indoor parking, Construction broke ground this month and is expected to finish in mid-2028. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mavrek Development & Fengate secured $130.4M construction debt from Affinius for Chicago West Loop tower
1000 West Jackson: 25-story, 380-unit multifamily; Fulton Market renaissance driving supply constraints
West Loop supply undershooting demand due to low deliveries; new construction justified by market fundamentals
stories.summary: Mavrek Development and Fengate Asset Management closed $130.4M in construction financing from Affinius Capital for a 25-story, 380-unit multifamily tower at 1000 West Jackson Street in Chicago's West Loop. The lender cited constrained multifamily supply and strong population growth tied to Fulton Market neighborhood renaissance and billions in real-estate investment over the past decade.
stories.impact: West Loop supply undershooting demand—a direct signal for developers to prioritize new unit delivery in this submarket. The Fulton Market live-work-play transformation continues to pull young professionals and household formation; expect sustained rent growth and lease-up velocity, supporting strong stabilized returns for 2027–2028 completions.

stories.title: Developer Launches Investor Offering for 465-Unit Boynton Beach Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Time Equities, Inc launched a $95.3 million tenant-in-common (“TIC”) investment offering for OCTAVIA, an eight-story, 465-unit Class A multifamily community under construction in downtown Boynton Beach, Florida. Having broken ground in September 2026, the development features 6,500 square feet of retail space, a 1,005-space parking garage, and approximately 50,000 square feet of private amenities. The investment structure includes senior positioning relative to approximately $34 million of sponsor equity and features an executed Tax Increment Financing (TIF) agreement expected to significantly lower real estate taxes for roughly ten years post-completion. Financial projections target an initial 5.75% annual current return, distributed quarterly, along with a planned refinancing to return a portion of invested capital on a tax-deferred basis. The OCTAVIA project team includes MSA Architects, ID & Design International, KAST Construction, and Kimley-Horn. The post Developer Launches Investor Offering for 465-Unit Boynton Beach Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Time Equities launched $95.3M TIC offering for 465-unit OCTAVIA in downtown Boynton Beach, Florida
Class A, 8-story, under construction; 5.75% current return; TIF abatement ~10 years post-completion
Senior debt + sponsor equity structure; retail, 1K parking spaces, 50K SF amenities; ground broken Sept 2026
stories.summary: Time Equities is raising $95.3M via a tenant-in-common (TIC) offering for OCTAVIA, a Class A 465-unit multifamily community under construction in downtown Boynton Beach, Florida. The eight-story project, which broke ground in September 2026, includes 6,500 SF of retail, a 1,005-space parking garage, and 50K SF of private amenities. The offering features an executed Tax Increment Financing (TIF) agreement for ~10 years of real-estate tax relief and targets a 5.75% annual current return.
stories.impact: TIF agreement materially improves underwriting economics in downtown Boynton Beach, compressing development hold-period IRRs and de-risking stabilization. The TIC structure signals strong co-investment appetite for Sun Belt infill multifamily; expect density and amenity-heavy projects in coastal South Florida downtown cores to attract institutional capital and justify higher construction costs.

stories.title: Manova Picks Up 1M-SF Spartanburg Logistics Facility
stories.excerpt: Manova Partners acquired Spartanburg 221, a 1,020,195-square-foot Class A+ logistics facility at 2536 Chesnee Highway in Spartanburg, S.C. The facility, completed in 2024, is 100% leased on a long-term, NNN basis to a single tenant, and the lease is backed by a guarantee from AA corporate credit. ESFM (Compass Group USA), which provides integrated facilities management and operational support services, is listed at the facility’s address. Spartanburg 221 was developed and sold by the Rockefeller Group. The property sits on 87 acres and offers 344 car parking spaces, 346 trailer storage spaces, 140 dock-high loading doors, 4 drive-in loading doors, and 40-foot clear height. The property is just a mile from I-85, which runs northeast through Charlotte, N.C., and southeast through Atlanta, GA. Since December 2024, Manova has transacted on logistics properties worth in excess of $600 million across three continents. The post Manova Picks Up 1M-SF Spartanburg Logistics Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Manova Partners acquired 1M SF Spartanburg logistics facility; 100% leased to AA-rated ESFM (Compass Group)
Spartanburg 221 completed 2024, 1M+ SF, $600M+ logistics portfolio acquired since Dec 2024 by Manova
Industrial deal; minimal multifamily relevance; logistics-driven supply-chain investment may pull labor to Spartanburg region
stories.summary: Manova Partners acquired Spartanburg 221, a 1,020,195-square-foot Class A+ logistics facility in Spartanburg, South Carolina, completed in 2024 and 100% leased on a long-term NNN basis to ESFM (Compass Group USA), backed by AA corporate credit. The property sits on 87 acres near I-85, with 344 parking spaces, 346 trailer storage spots, and 40-foot clear height. Manova has transacted on logistics assets worth $600M+ since December 2024.
stories.impact: Logistics-facility growth in Spartanburg signals supply-chain and distribution-hub expansion in the Carolinas corridor (I-85 northeast to Charlotte, southeast to Atlanta). This employment base growth may eventually drive multifamily demand; monitor for wage and job-formation data in Spartanburg and Greenville-Spartanburg region for downstream residential demand signals.

stories.title: CMBS Special Servicing Rate Reaches 13-Year High
stories.excerpt: The overall Trepp CMBS special servicing rate rose 33 basis points in August 2026 to 11.42%, reversing July’s decline and reaching its highest level since February 2013. A single $1.1-billion Hollywood studio-and-office loan, also the month’s largest new transfer to special servicing, drove mixed-use up 154 bps to 13.47%, Trepp reported. Office rose 32 bps to 16.90% on large CBD loan transfers, and retail also rose 32 bps to 13.60% on large mall and shopping center transfers. Lodging added 11 bps to reach 8.74%. Industrial and multifamily were the only property types to improve, falling seven bps to 1.27% and three bps to 8.37%, respectively. In all, the month’s transfers to special servicing totaled $3.16 billion across 32 whole loans, nearly double July’s. Transfers were concentrated in office. Several of the largest transfers ran out extension options, Trepp reported. Loans that cured, were modified and returned, or paid off were far smaller in aggregate, at roughly $500.7 million across 14 whole loans. Pictured: The CMBS loan on the Hyatt Regency New Orleans was among the large transfers to special servicing during August. The post CMBS Special Servicing Rate Reaches 13-Year High appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CMBS special servicing rate hit 11.42% in August 2026 (13-year high); +33 bps month-over-month
Office rose 32 bps to 16.90%; mixed-use soared 154 bps to 13.47%; multifamily fell 3 bps to 8.37%
Industrial & multifamily only sectors improving; $3.16B transfers to special servicing (vs. $500.7M cured/paid off)
stories.summary: The Trepp CMBS special servicing rate reached 11.42% in August 2026, its highest level since February 2013, driven by $3.16B in transfers to special servicing. Office spiked 32 bps to 16.90% on large CBD loan transfers; mixed-use surged 154 bps to 13.47% after a $1.1B Hollywood loan transfer. Multifamily, one of only two improving sectors, fell 3 bps to 8.37%, while industrial dropped 7 bps to 1.27%.
stories.impact: Multifamily's improving special-servicing rate (8.37%) and only-sector-improving credit profile signal stronger fundamentals and lower stress relative to office and mixed-use. Capital for multifamily debt and acquisitions should remain more accessible; use this window to refinance 2019–2021 bridge debt and lock in medium-term acquisition financing before interest-rate volatility or broader credit stress spreads to apartment loans.

stories.title: Shorenstein to Buy Fully Leased SoHo Office Property From Tishman Speyer
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer is selling the 12-story, 155,000-square-foot office building at 148 Lafayette Street in SoHo, at the corner of Lafayette and Howard streets, to Shorenstein Properties for around $135 million. The Real Deal was first to report the sale. The deal was repped by Newmark‘s Adam Spies, Doug Harmon, Adam Doneger, Marcella Fasulo, Avery Silverstein and Joshua King. Shorenstein outbid several institutional bidders, including private equity funds, for the building, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Tishman is selling the property on a quick turnaround at a sizable profit, having purchased the building from Epic in May 2025 for $105.5 million, with $68.3 million of that coming in the form of an acquisition loan from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies. Prior to the 2025 purchase, Tishman had not bought an office building anywhere in the U.S. since 2021, and had not purchased an office building in Manhattan since 2019, according to previous reporting in Commercial Observer. The $105.5 million purchase price in 2025 represented a decline from the $126.5 million Epic paid for the building in 2012. “148 Lafayette presented us with a compelling opportunity to capitalize on the strengthening New York City office leasing environment by acquiring a top-quality, boutique asset in one of the city’s most dynamic neighborhoods,” Albert Schmool, managing director at Tishman Speyer, said in a statement last year at the time of the purchase. The building contains 141,359 square feet of office space, which is 100 percent leased to tenants including investment firm General Catalyst, artificial intelligence code review firm Graphite, coworking firm WeWork, cosmetics company Charlotte Tilbury, digital picture frame company Aura Frames and consulting firm Keystone. There is also 13,454 square feet of retail on the ground and lower floors, which is also 100 percent leased to martial arts gym Five Points Academy and discount luxury retailer 260 Sample Sale. A
bullets: Shorenstein bought fully leased SoHo office building 148 Lafayette for ~$135M from Tishman Speyer
Tishman flipped for profit in 16 months: purchased May 2025 for $105.5M, sold ~$135M in Sept 2026
12-story, 155K SF, corner Lafayette & Howard; Tishman's first Manhattan office buy since 2019
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer sold the 12-story, 155,000-square-foot office building at 148 Lafayette Street (SoHo, corner of Lafayette and Howard) to Shorenstein Properties for approximately $135M. Tishman had acquired the property from Epic in May 2025 for $105.5M with $68.3M in Blackstone Real Estate Debt financing and flipped it in 16 months at a sizable profit, representing Tishman's first Manhattan office acquisition since 2019.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, the profitable flip and Shorenstein's outbid of PE funds signal renewed institutional appetite for stabilized, fully leased Manhattan office core—suggesting capital is rotating out of multifamily or taking tactical office plays. Monitor whether this reflects a diversification or signal of multifamily oversupply concerns in the same metros.

stories.title: Digital Financial Services Firm Zip Takes 13K SF at Rudin’s 41 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Zip, a digital banking company, is relocating to a new office space, Commercial Observer has learned. The firm, which specializes in credit and payment services, will move in April 2027 to Rudin’s 41 Madison Avenue in NoMad, where it will occupy 13,394 square feet across the entire 18th floor, according to the landlord. It’s unclear where Zip is moving from. Rudin declined to provide the asking rent for the 11-year lease, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown was $79.41 per square foot overall for the second quarter of 2026, while Class A office space averaged $97.22 per square foot during that time, according to Colliers data. “Modern tenants look for highly amenitized and thoughtfully designed spaces, making Rudin’s well-located and refreshed 41 Madison a prime destination for top-tier companies,” Robert Steinman, senior vice president of office leasing at Rudin, said in a statement. “Rudin has built a track record of offerings where businesses thrive, and Zip fits into that ecosystem seamlessly.” Steinman repped the landlord in-house alongside Craig Panzirer, senior vice president and head of office leasing at Rudin. Avison Young’s Joseph Gervino and Ryan Grecco represented Zip on this lease. Gervino and Grecco declined CO’s requests for comment. Opened in 1974, 41 Madison Avenue is a 42-story, 550,000-square-foot office property just northeast of Madison Square Park. The building recently underwent renovations including an expanded and fully redesigned lobby as well as a 7,000-square-foot conference space. Zip’s new lease brings the property to 93 percent leased, according to Rudin. Other tenants at 41 Madison Avenue include investment services firm Polar Asset Management Partners, investment bank BrightTower and talent services firm the Gersh Agency. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zip (digital banking/fintech) leased 13.4K SF entire 18th floor at Rudin's 41 Madison Avenue, NoMad
11-year lease; moving April 2027; Manhattan Midtown average Class A rent ~$97.22/SF in Q2 2026
Fintech/digital-services tenant; signals tech-sector footprint consolidation in Manhattan's mixed-use core
stories.summary: Zip, a digital financial services company specializing in credit and payment services, signed an 11-year lease for 13,394 square feet (entire 18th floor) at Rudin's 41 Madison Avenue in NoMad, relocating in April 2027. The asking rent was not disclosed, but Manhattan Class A office averaged $97.22 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing activity does not signal apartment demand, and fintech relocation is a sector-specific play, not a market-level demand signal for residential. However, continued fintech hiring and concentration in Manhattan's core could eventually pull high-income professionals to adjacent residential, particularly luxury units in NoMad and Flatiron.

stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Ian Slater of Compass’ Trove Partners
stories.excerpt: Founded in 2024 by real estate advisers Michael Koeneke and Ian Slater, Trove Partners is all about helping clients make a home in some of the most beautiful properties in New York City and the Hamptons in Long Island. Slater has spent 10 years in residential real estate advisory, becoming a top broker at Compass before teaming up with Koeneke to found Trove, a real estate team affiliated with the Compass brand. Now, Slater advises high-net-worth clients for that team and adds to his streak of selling more than $1 billion in the state. Commercial Observer caught up with Slater in September for a series called “Get to Know the Broker,” where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What has been the biggest deal of your career so far? Ian Slater: It’s a tie! There is a $29 million sale for a Greenwich Village townhouse, and the $29 million sale of an Uptown double-wide house. But, my team also sold a $112.5 million house in Southampton. What is your career Everest? It has been building Trove Partners from the ground up. We started with two people, and grew to the No. 1 team for our size (13) in New York state. Who has been your biggest influence? My husband, who I call my chief operating officer. He has encouraged me multiple times to take bigger risks than I thought I could. What’s your go-to Grubhub order? A Westville salad. Boring. What TV show are you currently binging? “The Beast in Me” and “The Pitt.” I tend to be years behind in television and movies. What is on your playlist? Podcasts on podcasts: “Pivot,” “The Daily,” “How I Built This,” “Hard Fork.” Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Trove Partners (Compass-affiliated) founded 2024 by Koeneke & Slater; focuses on NYC & Hamptons residential
Ian Slater career high: $112.5M Southampton house sale; $1B+ cumulative sales in New York state
Residential brokerage profile; no market-level development or investment implications
stories.summary: Trove Partners, founded in 2024 by real estate advisers Michael Koeneke and Ian Slater, is a Compass-affiliated team focused on high-net-worth residential sales in New York City and the Hamptons. Slater has sold over $1B in New York state assets, including a $112.5M Southampton house sale and two $29M transactions (Greenwich Village townhouse and Uptown double-wide), and has scaled Trove to 13 people.
stories.impact: No relevance to multifamily development. This is a luxury residential brokerage profile covering secondary-home and ultra-high-net-worth transactions in the Hamptons and Manhattan; does not inform multifamily demand, supply, capital, or cost analysis.
